result: C16 treatment substantially attenuated renal damage in Tg26 mice, as measured by lower serum creatinine, reduced albuminuria, reduced pPKR abundance, reduced urinary NGAL excretion, less glomerulosclerosis, less microtubular dilatation, and reduced fibrosis extent.
evaluation: All reviewers affirmed these findings. Reviewer 1 stated 'Treatment with C16 substantially attenuated renal damage in the Tg26 model as measured by urinary albumin/creatinine ratio, urinary NGAL/creatinine ratio and improvement in histology.' The editor noted 'A series of compelling experiments demonstrated that PKR inhibition can ameliorate HIVAN.' No concerns were raised about these core therapeutic efficacy findings.

result: A novel proximal tubule cell cluster (PT-Mito) was identified, characterized by higher expression of mitochondrial genes, comprising 3.1-5.8% of kidney cortex cells, confirmed by in situ hybridization and found in both mouse and human kidney data.
evaluation: Reviewer 1 noted 'The authors propose the existence of a novel injured proximal tubule cell-type characterized by the leak of mitochondrial transcripts into the nucleus (PT-Mito)' but expressed concern about 'limited resolution to determine whether mitochondrial RNA is present in the nuclei of injured PT cells.' Reviewer 2 stated 'The authors also identify a potential novel cell type within the kidney characterized by high expression of mitochondrial genes.' While reviewers acknowledged the identification, concerns about resolution and interpretation remain, and one reviewer requested quantification of cells with nuclear transcripts.

result: Mitochondrial dysfunction was identified as a central mechanism in Tg26 kidney disease, with downregulation of mitochondrial genes, reduced respiratory capacity in glomerular and proximal tubular tissues, and decreased mitochondrial complex I and II abundance, all of which were rescued by C16 treatment.
evaluation: Reviewers strongly supported these findings. Reviewer 1 stated 'The data in support of mitochondrial dysfunction are also robust and rely on combined evidence from downregulation of transcripts involved in oxidative phosphorylation, decreases in complex I and II as determined by immunoblot, and assessments of respiratory capacity in tubular and glomerular preparations.' The editor noted 'reversal of mitochondrial dysfunction (mainly confined to endothelial cells), a prominent feature shared in other kidney diseases.' Reviewer 2 affirmed 'mitochondrial dysfunction is induced in various cell types in Tg26 kidney.'

result: HIV-1 genes were expressed at high levels in podocytes in Tg26 mice, consistent with the notion that HIV-1 gene expression is particularly injurious to podocytes and with the prominent albuminuria observed.
evaluation: Reviewer 1 stated 'This data highlights that HIV transcripts are expressed in a subset of podocytes, consistent with the highly proteinuric disease seen in mouse and humans.' Reviewer 2 noted 'Other important advances include identifying the kidney cell types that express the HIV transgene.' The editor affirmed the study 'delineates the kidney cell types that express HIV genes and are injured in these HIV-transgenic mice.' No concerns were raised about these findings.

result: PKR pathway activation was demonstrated in Tg26 mice, with STAT3 identified as the most activated upstream regulator, confirmed by Western blot and immunohistochemistry showing increased phosphorylation, especially in injured proximal tubules (PT-Inj).
evaluation: Reviewer 2 stated 'They also identified STAT3 as a key upstream regulator of kidney injury in this model, which is consistent with previously published studies.' Reviewer 1 noted 'Some additional work has been done to show that C16 treatment results in a decrease in phospho-PKR, a readout of PKR inhibition. These changes strengthen the manuscript by providing some evidence for on-target activity for C16.' The findings are affirmed as consistent with prior literature.

result: Podocyte loss in Tg26 mice and recovery with C16 treatment were confirmed by p57 staining and podometric analysis, along with reversal of podocyte dedifferentiation markers.
evaluation: These findings are presented as confirmatory data supporting the therapeutic effect of C16. Reviewer 1 acknowledged the comprehensive analysis of podocyte injury. No specific concerns were raised about these histological and quantitative assessments of podocyte pathology and recovery.

result: An injured proximal tubule cluster (PT-Inj) was identified with increased cell numbers in Tg26 mice, showing gene expression profiles comparable to acute kidney injury and fibrosis models, with overlap between HIV-associated and ischemic injury pathways.
evaluation: Reviewer 1 noted 'transcripts were also seen in other tubular cells, notably intercalated cells, principal cells and injured proximal tubule cells' and acknowledged the comprehensive transcriptional analysis. The comparison to other injury models and the identification of shared pathways were not challenged by reviewers.

result: A putative fibrogenic pathway involving PKR-STAT3-PDGF-D-PDGFR-B was identified in injured proximal tubules, with PDGF-D upregulated in PT-Inj and downregulated by C16 treatment.
evaluation: This pathway identification is presented as a mechanistic finding supported by gene expression data, cell-cell interaction analysis, and immunohistochemistry. Reviewers did not challenge these findings, and they are consistent with the overall mechanistic framework of the study linking PKR to downstream injury pathways.

result: Pseudotime analysis and differential expression analysis revealed podocyte dedifferentiation in Tg26 mice, with activation of RHOGDI and coronavirus pathogenesis pathways, deactivation of integrin and actin cytoskeleton signaling, and upregulation of injury markers including Ccn2, Rbfox1, Itga4, Spp1, and Tgfb2.
evaluation: These detailed molecular characterizations of podocyte injury are part of the comprehensive transcriptional analysis that reviewers praised. Reviewer 1 stated 'The strengths of this study include the comprehensive transcriptional analysis of the Tg26 model.' No specific concerns were raised about these pathway and marker findings.

result: The authors acknowledge limitations including that the Tg26 model may not recapitulate all aspects of clinical HIVAN, gene expression changes after C16 treatment may include secondary effects, and the possibility of non-specific effects of C16.
evaluation: Reviewer 2 noted 'Though the HIV-transgenic model used in these studies results in a phenotype that is very similar to HIV-associated nephropathy in humans, the model has several limitations that may prevent direct translation to human disease.' Reviewer 1 stated 'The authors have revised the manuscript to acknowledge the potential limitations of the C16 tool compound used.' These limitations are appropriately acknowledged.
